theme: अभ्यंतर प्रेरणा और पाप / Inner impulse and moral action
context: After discussing svadharma, Arjuna asks a personal question: what impels a person to do wrong even when they do not wish to? The verse raises this question about action that feels compelled; Krishna’s answer follows in the next verse.
contextHindi: स्वधर्म की चर्चा के बाद अर्जुन एक निजी सवाल पूछते हैं: व्यक्ति न चाहने पर भी गलत काम करने के लिए किससे प्रेरित होता है? इस श्लोक में वे ऐसी बाध्यता का कारण पूछते हैं। कृष्ण इसका उत्तर अगले श्लोक में देते हैं।
sanskritDevanagari:
अर्जुन उवाच |
अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः |
अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः ||३-३६||
transliteration:
arjuna uvāca .
atha kena prayukto.ayaṃ pāpaṃ carati pūruṣaḥ .
anicchannapi vārṣṇeya balādiva niyojitaḥ ||3-36||

wordByWord.meaning: Arjuna speaks; the question is framed in the voice of a sincere seeker, not a dismissive skeptic.
then; it marks a direct follow-up question from the previous teaching.
by what; the question asks for the inner force behind action.
impelled, driven, set in motion; not a matter of mere excuse.
sin, morally harmful action, the deed that disturbs clarity and harms self and others.
moves, acts, indulges in; refers to ongoing conduct.
the human being; the person acting under inner force.
even without wishing it; the point is that wrongdoing is not always willfully chosen in the same way.
O descendant of Vrishni; Arjuna addresses Krishna in a familial and respectful way.
as if by force; the phrase stresses a feeling of compulsion and loss of agency.
engaged, constrained, directed by a force that is not fully under conscious control.

spokenHindi: अर्जुन अपने सवाल को सीधे बोलता है: अगर इंसान को अच्छाई समझ आती है, तो फिर वह बुरा क्यों करता है? यह सवाल बहुत गहरा है, क्योंकि हम अक्सर अपने व्यवहार को सिर्फ अपनी इच्छा से जोड़कर देखते हैं। लेकिन यहाँ अर्जुन कहता है कि कई बार मन चाहने के बावजूद भी किसी अज्ञात, शक्तिशाली दबाव के कारण गलत रास्ते पर चल पड़ता है। यह “बलात् इव” का भाव है—मानो अंदर का कोई जोर उसे खींच रहा है। यह बात हमें आत्म-जागरूकता की ओर ले जाती है। हम यह नहीं मानते कि मनुष्य पूरी तरह स्वतंत्र है, बल्कि यह समझते हैं कि भीतर के संस्कार, इच्छा, घबराहट, क्रोध और आसक्ति बहुत बार हमारे निर्णयों को ढक देते हैं। इसलिए सवाल यह है: हम अपने विवेक पर कितने नियंत्रण में हैं, और कौन-सा अंदर का बल हमें चलाता है?
clearEnglish: Arjuna’s question is not a trivial excuse. It is a serious inquiry into the psychology of moral failure. He recognizes that a person can know what is right and still find themselves drawn toward harm. The phrase “even without wishing it” is important: wrongdoing is not always a simple act of declared intention. It can feel like being driven by an inner force, as if the self is being pulled in a direction it does not freely endorse. This matters because it opens a path beyond moral shame alone. The problem is not merely that a person has bad intentions; it is that the mind can be overpowered by craving, irritation, fear, and habits. In that sense, the question is less about blame and more about the structure of the inner life.

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse frames sin as something a person does under compulsion, even when they do not wish it, “as if by force.” It asks for the causal factor behind this inner pull rather than assigning a final moral verdict.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: From the text we can infer that actions are influenced by inner forces not fully under direct conscious control. This is not a denial of responsibility; it is a call to look at desire, emotion, and patterning without judging oneself only at the surface level.

practicalApplication.label: Notice the trigger
practicalApplication.text: When you catch yourself acting in a way you later regret, pause and ask: what emotional trigger or thought pattern was in charge just before the action?

practicalApplication.label: Reduce compulsion
practicalApplication.text: Create a small pause between impulse and action—one breath, one sentence, or one question—so that desire does not become the automatic driver.

reflectionQuestion: What inner trigger most often makes me act against my better judgment, and what small pause can interrupt that pattern?
reflectionQuestionHindi: अंदर का कौन-सा कारण मेरे विवेक के खिलाफ सबसे ज़्यादा काम करता है, और उस पैटर्न को रोकने के लिए मैं एक छोटा सा विराम कैसे ले सकता हूँ?
